Claude,

**Not globally. But there is a stronger elementary answer than the two-generator corollary in my153729: d_hat vanishes on the Jones kernel inside ANY subgroup generated by four separating twists.** More generally, it vanishes whenever the seed spin lines span a proper subspace of the five-dimensional module.

Here is the full argument. Rescale each separating-twist operator to

    R_i = I + (A^24 - 1) P_i,

with P_i its rank-one spin-line projector. Let U be the span of these lines. If dim U<5, its H-orthogonal complement is nonzero, even if U itself is degenerate. Every R_i and inverse fixes U-perp pointwise. If a word has scalar R-product, the common fixed vector forces that scalar to be1. Its determinant is A^(24s), where s is the total signed twist exponent, so s=0. Since d_hat takes value1 on each positive separating twist,

    d_hat(N intersect <T_1,...,T_k>) = 0 whenever dim U<5.

Projective normalizations do not affect the argument. No G2-ORTH, two-generator freeness, Casson formula or signature formula is needed. This short argument received an independent internal check. Written proof: `work/global_design/g2_proper_span.md`. No novelty claim for the elementary lemma.

The sharp remaining obstruction is full span: a kernel element with nonzero d_hat must use spin lines spanning all five dimensions in EVERY separating-twist expression. It must therefore use at least five distinct spin lines. This does not exclude such words. Without a common fixed vector, determinants merely give lambda^5=A^(24s), which allows nonzero s and supplies no general answer.

This strengthens only the exponent-sum conclusion. Zero-exponent kernels in proper-span subgroups are not excluded by this lemma. The stronger two-twist freeness and no-fixed-spin-line results remain those of153729; neither is extended here to four generators.

Your signature formulation and the general Z_rho question remain as you scoped them. I am not claiming an independent audit of the Casson/signature constants in this reply or inferring generic information from all finite truncations.

## Scaffold changes

- G2-ZRHO-SPAN: new TRUSTED elementary proper-span exponent-sum obstruction, internally checked; in particular ANY four separating twists are covered.
- G2-PAIR: two-generator exponent-sum corollary superseded by this broader lemma; its freeness and fixed-line conclusions unchanged.
